{{Short description|Swiss-Austrian biochemist (1936–2015)}}
[[File:Gottfried Schatz 2001.jpg|thumb|150px|Gottfried Schatz]]
'''Gottfried Schatz'''  (18 August 1936 – 1 October 2015) was a Swiss-Austrian [[biochemist]].

== Life and career ==
Schatz was born in [[Strem]]. Upon obtaining his PhD in [[chemistry]] and [[biochemistry]] at the [[University of Graz]] ([[Austria]]), he did postdoctoral work at the [[University of Vienna]] and at "The Public Health Institute" of the City of New York. In 1968, he emigrated to the US in order to assume  a professorship [[Cornell University]] in [[Ithaca, New York|Ithaca]], [[New York (state)|New York]]. Six years later, he returned to Europe in order to join the  newly created [[Biozentrum University of Basel|Biozentrum]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/about-us/biozentrum-at-a-glance/history/emeriti/gottfried-schatz/ |title=Biozentrum History |publisher=Biozentrum.unibas.ch |date= |access-date=2015-10-04}}</ref> at the [[University of Basel]], which he chaired from 1983 to 1985, From 1984 to 1989 he was Secretary General of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO). After his retirement in 2000, he presided the ''Swiss Science and Technology Council'' (SSTC) until 2003. He is the author of more than 200 professional publications as well as of two books of essays on the broader implications of science. His scientific autobiography ''Interplanetary travels''<ref>Gottfried Schatz: ''Interplanetary travels'' – A scientific autobiography (Selected Topics in the History of Biochemistry, edited by G. Semenza and R. Jaenicke: Personal Recollections VI – Comprehensive Biochemistry Vol.41, Chapter 9, p. 449-530 – Elsevier Science B.V., 2000)</ref> was published in 2000.

Schatz died on 1 October 2015, aged 79.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.kleinezeitung.at/s/steiermark/graz/4834638/Wissenschaft_Biochemiker-Gottfried-Schatz-verstorben| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151002220929/http://www.kleinezeitung.at/s/steiermark/graz/4834638/Wissenschaft_Biochemiker-Gottfried-Schatz-verstorben| archive-date = 2015-10-02| title = Wissenschaft – Biochemiker Gottfried Schatz verstorben > Kleine Zeitung}} </ref>

== Work ==
{{more citations needed section|date=October 2014}}
Schatz played a leading role in elucidating the biogenesis of [[mitochondria]] and in discovering  [[mitochondrial DNA]].<ref>Ellen Haslbrunner, [[Hans Tuppy]] and Gottfried Schatz (1964 at the Institut for Biochemistry at the Medical Faculty of the [[University of Vienna]] in [[Vienna]], [[Austria]]): ''[http://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/emeritus/schatz/pdf/Schatz_BBRC_1964.pdf "Deoxyribonucleic Acid Associated with Yeast Mitochondria"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080910184516/http://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/emeritus/schatz/pdf/Schatz_BBRC_1964.pdf |date=2008-09-10 }}'' (PDF) Biochem. Biophys. Res. Commun. 15, 127 – 132.</ref> He recognized that this DNA encoded only a small number of mitochondrial proteins which was decisive for his further research on the import of proteins into the mitochondria and the degradation of proteins within these organelles. Schatz discovered a complex transport system that recognizes mitochondrial proteins made in the cytoplasm by specific signals attached to these proteins and then transfers them into the mitochondria. This system comprises two protein complexes, [[TIM/TOM complex|TOM and TIM]], which are localized in the outer and inner mitochondrial membranes respectively. Mutations in these complexes can disrupt protein import and cause illnesses such as the neurodegenerative [[Mohr-Tranebjaerg syndrome]], which leads to deafness. Schatz also demonstrated that the energy-requiring protease Lon regulates protein turnover within the mitochondria, thus maintaining the integrity and the proper functioning of mitochondrial DNA. Gottfried Schatz is the author of more than 200 scientific publications, three volumes of essays, an [[autobiography]] and a novel. His books have appeared in English, French, Greek and Czech translation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kleinezeitung.at/s/steiermark/graz/4834638/Wissenschaft_Biochemiker-Gottfried-Schatz-verstorben|title=Wissenschaft – Biochemiker Gottfried Schatz verstorben|work=Kleine Zeitung|date=2 October 2015 }}</ref>
